To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the outage probability and throughput performance of wireless powered relaying systems can be analyzed using finite block length coding theory, and that in short codeword scenarios, the outage probability/ throughputs of the systems with time switching relaying or power splitting relaying are comparable.

(i) the outage probability of the joint energy-information transfer systems decreases with increasing codeword length; (ii) the outage probability is higher for the case with short codeword length than for the case with long codeword length, and the outage probability gap increases with decreasing signal to noise ratios; (iii) the throughput is higher for the cases with short and long codeword lengths than for the case of no energy transfer, and the throughput gain increases with decreasing codeword
the finite block length codes are important for wireless powered relaying in the scenarios with short codeword length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the outage probability/ throughput of amplify and forwarding relaying with finite codewords.
finite block length analysis of wireless information and energy harvesting relaying.
the outage probability and throughput of wireless powered relaying with short codeword lengths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outage probability/ throughput of the system is a function of the codeword block length and the energy transfer efficiency of the system.
in the short codeword case, the outage probability of a relay network with energy and information transfer is higher than that of a network with only information transfer.
, the outage performance of the joint energy-information transfer systems is improved by using the power splitting relays and increasing the number of time slots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the outage probability/ throughput of the system is affected by the codeword lengths and the energy and information transfer protocols.
the outage probability/ throughput of the joint energy-information transfer system can be improved by using short codewords in the cases with high signal to noise ratio and low codeword length.
we provide a novel analysis for wireless powered relaying with short codeword lengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of short codewords, the time switching protocol is more efficient compared to the power splitting protocol.
the finite block length codes should be used in delay constrained scenarios to achieve a reliable performance.
the outage probability/ throughput of the joint wireless energy and information transfer system can be reduced significantly by increasing the number of bits per symbol.
